draft.title: Religious missions
card: A mission was a settlement run by a church. In colonial Australia, churches set up missions for Aboriginal people.
The main aim was to convert Aboriginal people to Christianity. Missionaries also wanted to change how people lived, such as their clothing, work and daily routines.
Some missions gave shelter, food and protection from violence. Some people chose to live on them for these reasons.
Missions often disrupted culture and language. Missionaries could discourage the use of Aboriginal languages and ceremonies, and could break the links people had with their Country.
draft.remember: Missions could give shelter, but they set out to change Aboriginal people's lives and often harmed culture and language.

a.q: What was the main aim of churches that set up missions for Aboriginal people?
opts: To convert people to Christianity and change how they lived
To return land to Aboriginal people and protect ceremonies
To train Aboriginal people to run the colonial government
To collect taxes from Aboriginal communities for the church
a.why: Churches ran missions to convert people to Christianity and to change how they lived. Protecting ceremonies is the opposite of what often happened, because missions could discourage culture and language.
a.clue: Think about what the word convert means.

b.q: A family moves to a church mission in the 1870s because they need food and safety. Over the years, the children are discouraged from speaking their language. What does this case show about missions?
opts: Missions could give shelter but also disrupt culture
Missions gave only harm, so no one chose to live there
Missions gave shelter and left language unchanged
Missions were run by the government to hold people in jail
b.why: The family found shelter and food, but their children were pushed away from their language. This shows that missions could do both. The option saying no one chose them is wrong, because some people did live on missions for shelter.
b.clue: Look for the answer that has both the shelter and the loss.

a.best: To convert people to Christianity and change how they lived

b.best: Missions could give shelter but also disrupt culture
